minutes.headline: Zoning board's motion to grant a solar array permit on an undersized lot failed, short of the four votes needed.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued a hearing on a ground-mounted solar array at 191 Cross Road on a lot far smaller than the required acreage. The applicant's engineer presented a revised three-tracker layout, setbacks and 3D sight-line renderings. A motion to grant was debated over precedent and the bylaw's intent, then failed on a roll vote. The board then discussed alternate and regular member vacancies and an upcoming meeting.

public_comment.topic: The applicant's representative argued the bylaw targets massive commercial arrays, that two of the three trackers are not visible from abutters, and that the property should be judged on its merits.
An abutter said every array would be visible from his backyard despite the line-of-sight claims.
A Leominster Road resident questioned the array width arithmetic against the east buffer zone; the engineer clarified the spacing.

votes.motion: Grant the permit for the reduced structures as positioned, with a provision for two smaller trees to be planted to screen.
votes.outcome: failed; the chair called three ayes and two noes, short of the four of five required

decisions.decision: The board will wait to hear whether the earlier alternate applicant is still interested before seeking other candidates; the secretary was asked to contact him.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals failed to grant a permit for a ground-mounted solar array at 191 Cross Road; three voted yes and two no, short of the four needed.
The motion would have allowed the reduced structures as positioned, with two smaller trees planted for screening.
The applicant's engineer presented a revised three-tracker layout, setbacks and 3D sight-line images for a lot far smaller than the required acreage.
The applicant's representative argued the bylaw targets massive commercial arrays; an abutter said the arrays would still be visible from his backyard.
The board will wait to hear whether an earlier alternate applicant is still interested, and the secretary was asked to contact him.

why_it_matters: The vote shows how the board weighs the minimum lot size in the zoning bylaw against a small residential solar project, which bears on what neighbors and property owners can expect for similar arrays.
Open member and alternate seats matter because a permit needs four of five votes, so a missing member can leave an applicant short.
watch_next: The board's upcoming meeting on the 10th, mentioned at the close of the session.
